blocks.orig: Mount Kilimanjaro is Africa’s highest mountain and the tallest free-standing mountain in the world. Each year it attracts thousands of climbers and adventurers from all over the world. Climbing Mount Kilimanjaro is like walking from the tropical to the arctic in just one week. It is a real challenge due to the altitude and the rate of ascent, but also extremely rewarding.
blocks.html: Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa and the tallest free-standing mountain anywhere on earth. Every year, thousands of climbers and adventurers from across the globe are drawn to it. Climbing Mount Kilimanjaro is a bit like walking from the tropics to the arctic in a single week. The altitude and the speed of the ascent make it a genuine challenge, but one that is hugely rewarding.

blocks.orig: In 1987 UNESCO listed Mount Kilimanjaro as World Heritage Site because of its natural beauty. The variety of vegetation and landscapes is amazing due to the mountains location and immense height. From tropical rainforest with monkeys and birds to the ‘Roof of Africa’ where you see glaciers and an impressive snow-capped summit. On a classic climb you pass through one vegetation zone every day and a half.
blocks.html: UNESCO added Mount Kilimanjaro to its World Heritage list in 1987 on account of its natural beauty. Thanks to the mountain's position and enormous height, the range of vegetation and scenery is remarkable: from tropical rainforest full of monkeys and birds up to the ‘Roof of Africa’, with its glaciers and an impressive snow-capped summit. On a classic climb you cross one vegetation zone roughly every day and a half.

blocks.orig: The thrill of reaching the top of the Mount Kilimanjaro after days of walking is amazing. At the summit you are rewarded with breathtaking views of the African savannah and Rift Valley. Climbing Mount Kilimanjaro is absolutely an experience of a life time!
blocks.html: Reaching the top of Mount Kilimanjaro after days of walking is an incredible thrill. At the summit your reward is a breathtaking view over the African savannah and the Rift Valley. Climbing Mount Kilimanjaro really is a once-in-a-lifetime experience!

blocks.orig: Everyone can climb Africa’s highest mountain!
blocks.html: Anyone can climb the highest mountain in Africa!

blocks.orig: Do you have the dream of climbing Mount Kilimanjaro but wonder if you can make it? Climbing Mount Kilimanjaro is certainly a challenge, but you don’t need to be an experienced climber to reach its summit. If you are healthy and fit it is absolutely within reach. We have an experienced and professional team that can bring you to the top safely.
blocks.html: Is climbing Mount Kilimanjaro a dream of yours, but you are not sure you can manage it? It is certainly demanding, yet you need no climbing experience to reach the summit. If you are healthy and fit, it is well within your reach. Our experienced, professional team will get you to the top safely.

blocks.orig: That is why 95% of our guests reach the top of Africa’s highest mountain. There are many things you can do to increase your chances to reach the summit and to make sure you enjoy the trek. One of the things is buying good gear and practice hikes in your home country a few months before your departure. Since altitude sickness is the main reason people fail to reach the top, it’s important to take your time. Give your body time to acclimatize. Check out below which climbing route fits you best.
blocks.html: That is why 95% of our guests make it to the top of Africa’s highest mountain. There is a lot you can do to improve your odds of reaching the summit and to make sure you enjoy the trek. Buying good gear and doing practice hikes at home a few months before you leave is one of them. As altitude sickness is the main reason people fail to reach the top, it is important not to rush. Let your body acclimatise. Below you can see which climbing route suits you best.

blocks.orig: Porters make it possible for you to climb Kilimanjaro. They carry all your food, gear and supplies and are an essential part of your mountain experience. Without their commitment and hard work, you are not able to climb and enjoy the magnificence of Kilimanjaro. Unfortunately local porters are often exploited and have poor working conditions. That is why we support our porters, this helps improving the working conditions of the porters on Kilimanjaro. If you book a climbing Kilimanjaro trip with us, you automatically contribute to a fair treatment of Kilimanjaro porters.
blocks.html: It is the porters who make your Kilimanjaro climb possible. They carry all your food, gear and supplies and are a vital part of your time on the mountain. Without their dedication and hard work you simply could not climb Kilimanjaro or enjoy its magnificence. Sadly, local porters are often exploited and work under poor conditions. That is why we support our porters, which helps to improve working conditions for porters on Kilimanjaro. When you book a Kilimanjaro climb with us, you automatically contribute to fair treatment of the mountain's porters.

blocks.orig: Once you have decided to climb Kilimanjaro, the main question now is which route you should choose. There are seven different routes to the summit. They all vary in length, difficulty, scenery, traffic, accommodation and other aspects. Based on our experience we advise you to choose one of the first 3 routes.
blocks.html: Once you have made up your mind to climb Kilimanjaro, the big question is which route to take. Seven different routes lead to the summit, and they differ in length, difficulty, scenery, traffic, accommodation and more. Based on our experience, we recommend picking one of the first 3 routes.

blocks.orig:
Machame route
This is one the most popular climbs due to the diversity and beauty of the route. You walk from green rainforest to the beautiful Shira Plateau and the rock lava slopes. The trail circles around the mountain with spectacular views. Another advantage is the gradual ascend, so people have more time to acclimatize, which increases the success rate. The Machame route, also known as the “Whiskey route” has an average to high success rate, especially if you choose the 7 days itinerary. This route is less expensive than most others but has the disadvantage to be quite busy.
blocks.html:
Machame route
The variety and beauty of this route make it one of the most popular climbs. You walk from green rainforest to the lovely Shira Plateau and the lava-rock slopes. The trail curves around the mountain and offers spectacular views. A further plus is the gradual ascent, which gives people more time to acclimatise and so raises the success rate. The Machame route, also called the “Whiskey route”, has an average to high success rate, particularly on the 7-day itinerary. It costs less than most other routes, but the downside is that it can be rather busy.

blocks.orig:
Lemosho route
This route is known for its varied and breathtaking scenery. The Lemosho route is also less crowded with climbers than some of Kilimanjaro’s longer established routes. Although Memosho is a more expensive route, it gives climber plenty of time to acclimatize properly. This route is remote and beautiful. High success rate.
blocks.html:
Lemosho route
The Lemosho route is famous for its varied and breathtaking scenery. It also sees fewer climbers than some of the longer-established routes on Kilimanjaro. Although Memosho costs more, it allows climbers ample time to acclimatise properly. A remote and beautiful route with a high success rate.

blocks.orig:
Marangu route
The Maranga route is the second most popular route and cheapest one to reach the top of the Kilimanjaro. It is the only route that uses the same trail to ascend and descend and offers hut accommodation (camping is not allowed). This route, nicknamed the “Coca-Cola” route, has a reputation of being one of the easiest paths on the mountain. It certainly is the shortest Kilimanjaro route, yet it gives climbers less time to acclimatize and clarifies the lower success rate. Marangu is unfortunately less scenic than other routes and can be crowded during the peak season.
blocks.html:
Marangu route
The Maranga route is the second most popular and the cheapest way to the top of Kilimanjaro. It is the only route that ascends and descends along the same trail, and the only one with hut accommodation (camping is not permitted). Nicknamed the “Coca-Cola” route, it has a reputation as one of the easiest paths on the mountain. It is certainly the shortest Kilimanjaro route, but that leaves climbers less time to acclimatise, which explains its lower success rate. Unfortunately Marangu is also less scenic than other routes and can get crowded in peak season.

blocks.orig:
Northern Circuit route
The Northern Circuit is the longest Kilimanjaro route and also one of the most beautiful and enjoyable ones. The route circles around the mountain and offers great views from all sides of the Kilimanjaro. The summit success rate is very high, as the route is long and gives lots of time to acclimatize. This is a great route for those who want to experience all the beauty Kilimanjaro has to offer and have time and money.
blocks.html:
Northern Circuit route
The Northern Circuit is the longest route up Kilimanjaro and also one of the most beautiful and enjoyable. It loops right around the mountain, giving superb views of Kilimanjaro from every side. Because the route is long and allows plenty of time to acclimatise, the summit success rate is very high. It is an excellent choice if you want to experience everything Kilimanjaro has to offer and have both the time and the money.

blocks.orig:
Shira route
This route is very scenic, but also expensive and difficult. We only advise experienced climbers to choose this route due to the high starting point of the route, which gives the body less time to acclimatize.
blocks.html:
Shira route
This is a very scenic route, but also an expensive and difficult one. Because it starts at a high point, the body gets less time to acclimatise, so we only recommend it to experienced climbers.

blocks.orig:
Rongai route
This route suits the more experienced climbers. Since the ascent and descent are on opposite sides, climbers can see both sides of Kilimanjaro. At the same time this additional transport, to reach the other side, makes the climb more expensive. Rongai is one of the quieter routes, but also dryer and less scenic.
blocks.html:
Rongai route
This route is better suited to more experienced climbers. As you go up one side and come down the other, you get to see both faces of Kilimanjaro. The extra transport needed to reach the far side does make the climb more expensive, though. Rongai is among the quieter routes, but it is also drier and less scenic.

blocks.orig:
Umbwe route
This route is known as the steepest Kilimanjaro route. Due to its rapid ascend the success rate is much lower. We advise only experienced mountain climbers, who are used to high altitudes, to climb this route.
blocks.html:
Umbwe route
Umbwe is known as the steepest route on Kilimanjaro. Its rapid ascent means the success rate is far lower. We only recommend this route to experienced mountaineers who are used to high altitudes.

blocks.orig: My name is Phabian, I am a guide and for over 16 years I lead people to the summit. The most popular route is the Lemosho route, due to the breathtaking scenery and views. If you are fit and well prepared, you can also climb the Marangu-, Machame-, and Northern Circuit Route.
blocks.html: I am Phabian, a guide, and for more than 16 years I have been leading people to the summit. The Lemosho route is the most popular, thanks to its breathtaking scenery and views. If you are fit and well prepared, the Marangu, Machame and Northern Circuit routes are also open to you.

blocks.orig: How long to stay? The duration of the climbing route + 2 nights (arrival and departure day).
blocks.html: How long should you stay? The length of your climbing route + 2 nights (the day you arrive and the day you leave).

blocks.html: Which hotel? Our guests' favourite place to stay is the Weru Weru River Lodge, for its warm, friendly service, delicious food and beautiful setting with a pool beside a coffee plantation.

blocks.orig: You can climb Kilimanjaro any time of the year, but the best conditions to climb Africa’s highest peak, are during the months June till mid-March (except November). February is the best month since the temperature is high and the changes or rainfall low. The rainy season starts from mid-March till June and the month November. However there are people who choose to climb Kilimanjaro in April or November since it is quite and less crowded on the trails.
blocks.html: Kilimanjaro can be climbed in any month, but the best conditions for tackling Africa’s highest peak are from June until mid-March (November excepted). February is the finest month of all, with high temperatures and little chance of rain. The rainy season runs from mid-March to June and again in November. Even so, some people deliberately climb Kilimanjaro in April or November, because the trails are quiet and far less crowded.

blocks.html: At 5,895 metres (19, 341 ft), Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest free-standing mountain in the world. Climbing it is an adventure you will never forget. As people say: “You should do that ones in your life!”
